name: Microsoft for Education Daily
tldr: Windows' Release Preview brings small wins for classrooms, Microsoft apologised for the outage that hit schools, and Xbox's 25th brings a free Minecraft skin.
window: Window: the 24 hours to 05:45 AEDT, Sat 14 Nov 2026 (Thursday 12 to Friday 13 Nov in the US).
notes: Windows' pointer indicator, Sticky Keys prompt, Narrator math languages, Windows Hello brightening, Miracast fix and hybrid web sign-in are in Release Preview (KB5132057) for Insiders, rolling out gradually; the BitLocker PIN is in the Beta (26H1) channel. GitHub's AI Scan API and Front Door's token checks are in preview; Word's change starts in December.

The KLS post dates from 21 Oct; Research Focus #98 (12 Nov) featured it. The outage statement is Microsoft's (on X, quoted by Mashable); recovery was broad but not complete at publication. Known-issue details are as reported by BleepingComputer.
Screenshots are the publishers' public pages as captured on 14 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

post.text:
SMALL WINS. 🎓

The last 24h at Microsoft for education:
- Narrator reads maths in 8 more languages (Release Preview)
- Sticky Keys: switch it off from the pop-up
- Old Word 2010 docs may reflow from Dec: save a PDF
- Microsoft apologised for the outage that hit schools

stories.title: Windows' new pointer indicator helps people with low vision find the mouse
stories.summary: In the latest Windows 11 Release Preview update (KB5132057, versions 25H2 and 26H2), a new pointer indicator makes the mouse pointer easier to locate. Turn it on in Settings > Accessibility > Mouse pointer and touch, then toggle it with Windows + Ctrl + Shift + X.
stories.for: Students and staff with low vision

stories.title: Turn off Sticky Keys straight from the pop-up when it's triggered by accident
stories.summary: If someone accidentally triggers the shortcut for Sticky Keys, Filter Keys or Toggle Keys, they can now turn it off directly from the prompt that appears. It's in the same Windows 11 Release Preview update.

stories.title: Narrator reads maths aloud in eight more languages
stories.summary: Narrator's math reading now supports Greek, Hungarian, Indonesian, Norwegian (Bokmål), Polish, Russian, Swedish and Vietnamese, in the Windows 11 Release Preview update.
stories.for: Students who use a screen reader

stories.title: Windows Hello can brighten the screen to recognise your face in a dark room
stories.summary: Windows Hello facial recognition can now briefly brighten the screen to help you sign in in a dark or dimly lit room, for example with the lights down for a video. Turn it on under Settings > Accounts > Sign-in options > Facial recognition.

stories.title: Word is retiring some Compatibility Mode options, so old documents may reflow
stories.summary: Microsoft is retiring a set of compatibility options in the Word desktop app for documents in Compatibility Mode. Files created or last saved in Word 2010 or earlier may reflow, change spacing or page count, or move images; Microsoft suggests exporting them to PDF first. Word for Windows from December 2026, Mac in early 2027.

stories.title: A Miracast fix stops wireless casting dropping to a lower resolution
stories.summary: The Windows 11 Release Preview update fixes an issue that might make Miracast connections default to a lower resolution with certain wireless display receivers, handy when casting to a classroom screen.
stories.for: Teachers who cast to a screen

stories.title: Passwordless web sign-in comes to Microsoft Entra hybrid joined PCs
stories.summary: Web sign-in now works on Entra hybrid joined PCs as well as Entra joined ones: at the lock screen, sign in without a password using a FIDO2 security key, a passkey on your phone or a Temporary Access Pass, and on-premises file shares keep working.

stories.title: Staff without admin rights can set their own BitLocker preboot PIN
stories.summary: In Windows 11 Insider Beta (26H1) build 28020.3532, standard users on managed PCs can add a BitLocker TPM+PIN themselves when prompted, once IT sets the existing BitLocker policies in Intune or another management tool. Microsoft says to target only a test group with the feature for now.

stories.title: Switch GitHub's AI Scan for repositories on or off with the REST API
stories.summary: Organization owners and security managers can now turn code scanning's AI Scan for repositories on or off with the REST API, at organization and repository level, so it can be rolled out by script. Turning it on doesn't start a scan, and each scan uses GitHub Code Security AI credits.

stories.title: Azure Front Door Premium checks client certificates, and Entra tokens in preview
stories.summary: Mutual TLS (client certificate authentication) is generally available on Azure Front Door Premium, and JWT validation, which checks Microsoft Entra ID tokens at the edge before requests reach your apps, is in public preview.
stories.status: mTLS GA; token checks in preview

stories.title: A 31-year-old maths problem, the KLS conjecture, has been solved with human-directed AI
stories.summary: A Microsoft researcher and a collaborator proved the Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits conjecture, open since 1995, in a process where AI systems explored possibilities while the researchers steered the search. The proof was independently validated and formally verified; Microsoft Research's latest roundup featured it.

stories.title: Microsoft apologises for the Microsoft 365 outage that disrupted schools worldwide
stories.summary: Microsoft said it is deeply sorry for the outage that hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot on 12-13 November, that it was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI agents, and that it will publish a full post-incident report. It reported broad recovery while restoring remaining customers.
stories.for: Everyone on campus, and school IT

stories.title: November's Windows update: some documents may not print, and KMS activation commands can fail
stories.summary: Microsoft confirmed that after the November security updates, documents with zero-size images (such as some watermarks) may fail to print, and slmgr commands that set up KMS activation or product keys can fail with error 0x80041008. Already activated PCs stay activated, and a fix for activation is due in the coming days, BleepingComputer reports.

stories.title: A free Xbox-green Minecraft skin for Xbox's 25th anniversary
stories.summary: Minecraft players can claim a free OG Green Character Creator item in the Minecraft dressing room until 10 December at 10am PT. It needs Minecraft: Bedrock Edition (sold separately), one per account.

stories.title: Flight Simulator 2024 gets four throwback Xbox liveries, including a hot air balloon
stories.summary: For Xbox's 25th, four commemorative liveries for the Boeing 737 MAX, XCub, Hot Air Balloon and Skyship 600 are available automatically to all Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 owners.

stories.title: Xbox Insiders can shuffle Home backgrounds and put the Guide on the left or right
stories.summary: Xbox Insiders can save favourite dynamic backgrounds and shuffle them at each sign-in, hourly, daily or weekly, choose which side the Guide opens on, and sort disc-based games with digital licences into their own library category. Alpha Skip-Ahead members get them first.

transcript.t: This is the Microsoft for Education Daily, for Saturday.
Here's your day in Microsoft updates, in 3 minutes flat.
Small wins. In Windows' Release Preview, a new pointer indicator helps students with low vision find the mouse.
Hit Sticky Keys by accident? Turn it off right from the pop-up.
For students, Narrator now reads maths aloud in 8 more languages, from Greek and Polish to Vietnamese.
Lights down for a video? Windows Hello can now briefly brighten your screen, so face sign-in still works.
Teachers, files last saved in Word 2010 or earlier may reflow from December.
Save a PDF first.
Casting to the class screen? A Miracast fix stops it dropping resolution.
For school IT, Release Preview lets hybrid joined PCs sign in with a security key, no password.
And in the Beta channel, staff without admin rights can set their own BitLocker start-up PIN.
University dev teams can now switch GitHub's AI code scanning on across repositories with a script, in preview.
Running campus web apps? Azure Front Door Premium now checks client certificates, and in preview, Entra tokens too.
In Microsoft Research's latest roundup, a 31-year-old maths problem, the KLS conjecture, has been solved.
A Microsoft researcher and a collaborator proved it, with AI exploring ideas while they steered the search.
The fine print? Microsoft says it's deeply sorry for the outage that hit Outlook, Teams, and schools worldwide.
And after November's update, some Word documents may not print, and KMS activation commands can fail.
After hours, for Xbox's 25th, claim a free Xbox green Minecraft skin until December 10.
Flight Simulator pilots get four throwback liveries automatically, even one for the hot air balloon.
And Xbox Insiders can shuffle Home backgrounds, and put the Guide on the left or right.
Bumpy week? Find the pointer, save the PDF, then go play. Small wins.
Day after day, the updates keep stacking up.
Some of it's shipped. The rest is on its way.
One day, all of this. Tomorrow, probably more.
This has been the Microsoft for Education Daily.
See you tomorrow.
